answer: An identity buys certification in the cedar registry from a falcon certifier, who posts 500 bond and certifies ten per epoch. The applicant locks 60 and pays 30, so one identity costs 90, bond returned if clean. A pearl log publishes certifications for recount. A proven fake burns its 60-credit bond, and its falcon loses 100 and two slots, forcing a fresh 250-credit falcon every ten fakes. The thousandth fake costs 340; 1,000 fakes cost 115,000. A rented falcon ring fails: a falcon with no work history is slashed and its certifications voided. An honest agent pays 90 once.
